domain_description: How teachers actually get better at the job — not training days that vanish on Monday morning. Coaching conversations, lesson study cycles, observation routines, structured inquiry, and PD design that respects what we know about adult learning. All interventions cross-referenced to peer-reviewed meta-analyses where one exists. We have curated the Manning catalogue here for relevance, leaving out internal QA tools and operational utilities that do not function as teaching interventions.

skills.description: Design PD sessions that actually change practice — built around the four IMTP mechanisms (Insight, Motivation, Techniques, Practice) rather than the usual 'sit and get'. Sustained over time, with deliberate practice between sessions and clear classroom techniques teachers can use on Monday.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Designing mechanism-rich PD (per Sims, Fletcher-Wood et al. 2025's IMTP theory: Insight, Motivation, Techniques, Practice) requires the facilitator to understand cognitive- and behavioural-science principles, not just CPD buzzwords. No materials cost; the lift is on the person designing and running the PD. Sims's finding is that average PD has d=0.05 — well-designed PD has to do something different to land.

skills.description: Structure coaching conversations that actually move practice — observation evidence, focused goals, specific techniques to try, and follow-up — instead of vague 'how did that feel?' chats. Built on Knight-style instructional coaching with a feedback loop that respects teacher autonomy.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Trained coaches, scheduled time release for both coach and coachee, and sustained contact over time. One of the more expensive PD interventions per teacher — but Kraft, Blazar & Hogan found that pairing coaching with group training amplifies effects, and that quality of focus matters more than raw contact hours. The d=0.49 is the effect on teacher instruction (the direct target); the downstream effect on student achievement is more modest (d=0.18). Plan accordingly.

skills.description: Design a full lesson study cycle — shared learning goal, collaborative planning, research lesson with observers, structured debrief, refined re-teach — built on the Japanese jugyou kenkyuu tradition rather than a one-off 'observe each other once' exercise.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Requires sustained time for the full cycle (planning, research lesson, observer debrief, refined re-teach), pairs or triads of teachers freed up together, and continuity across terms. The g=0.47 reflects teacher self-efficacy outcomes — the proximal target lesson study reliably moves. Be transparent about the distal evidence: Bradbury et al. 2021 (EEF trial, 181 English primary schools) found null on student attainment overall, with heterogeneous effects by school size. Lesson study delivers on teacher growth more reliably than on direct student outcomes.

skills.description: Design a structured teacher inquiry cycle — Timperley's spiral or an action-research loop — that starts from real student-learning evidence, moves through collaborative interpretation, agreed action, and re-measurement, instead of vague 'reflection' that never closes the loop.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Real inquiry cycles take terms or years to run properly: a full loop from collecting student-learning evidence, interpreting it as a team, agreeing action, and re-measuring impact. Ansyari et al. found heterogeneity: effects are largest when collaboration is genuine and leadership actively supports the inquiry. The honest comparison: generic teacher PD sits around d=0.05–0.09 (Sims 2025; 2025 128-study meta-analysis); disciplined inquiry with collaboration and support reaches g=0.41 — but only when the structural conditions are in place.

skills.description: Design observation protocols with subject-specific look-fors and a feedback structure that supports growth rather than judgement — paired observation, non-evaluative debrief, agreed next step. The observation is for the observed teacher's learning, not the observer's checklist.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: No materials cost. The lift is on developing genuinely useful look-fors (subject-specific, behavioural, not vague 'engagement'), a non-evaluative feedback structure, and protected time for paired observation and debrief. Less expensive than full instructional coaching (no external coach required) but the same boundary condition applies: Bradbury et al. 2021's EEF trial (181 English primary schools) found that low-stakes peer observation with light protocols produced no measurable effect on student attainment. Quality of the protocol and the feedback conversation are what carry the d=0.49 — not observation alone.

skills.description: Build the specific knowledge teachers need to teach their subject well — common misconceptions, productive analogies, the order to introduce ideas, the bits that always trip students up. Shulman's PCK: not just knowing the content, knowing how to teach it.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: PCK is the most subject-specific form of teacher learning, which makes it expensive: subject-specialist PD facilitators (often hard to find at scale), sustained engagement, and a separate PD track per subject area. Lynch et al.'s d=0.52 is the proximal effect on teacher knowledge — the construct PCK directly grows. The downstream effect on student achievement is more modest (d=0.21). Hill, Rowan & Ball 2008 found teachers with stronger Mathematical Knowledge for Teaching produced student gains equivalent to 2–3 extra weeks of instruction per year. Evidence is strongest in STEM; PCK in language and social-science subjects is less well meta-analysed.
